title: Umag Travel Guide: Beaches, Parking & Where to Stay
metaDescription: Plan your trip to Umag, Croatia. Get practical details on driving routes, where to stay, parking, family resorts, and the best times to visit.
intro:
Umag is the northernmost coastal town in Istria, making it the first stop for visitors driving from Central Europe. It caters heavily to resort-style tourism, offering large hotel complexes, camping grounds, and extensive sports facilities, most notably the ATP Croatia Open tennis tournament. The coastline features paved sunbathing terraces, rocky coves, and pine forests backing directly onto the sea.

Peak season runs from late June to August, bringing high temperatures and the main tennis crowds in July. September is quieter with the sea still warm enough for swimming, while winter sees most tourist facilities close. Umag suits families and active travelers who prioritize convenient beach access and sports over extensive historical sightseeing.

areas.name: Umag Centre & Old Town
areas.parking: Paid public lots outside the pedestrian peninsula
areas.summary: The historic heart of Umag sits on a small peninsula. It offers narrow streets, restaurants, and a marina, but lacks the large resort pools and direct beach access found further north.

areas.name: Punta
areas.bestFor: Proximity to both the centre and beaches
areas.parking: On-street paid parking and private hotel lots
areas.beach: Immediate access to concrete and rocky beaches
areas.summary: A residential and hotel area just north of the marina. It connects the town centre to the northern resorts via a coastal promenade, balancing convenience with beach access.

areas.name: Stella Maris & Katoro
areas.bestFor: Families, tennis fans, and resort holidays
areas.parking: Large dedicated lots for resort and day guests
areas.beach: Immediate access to Laguna (pebbles/sand) and Polynesia
areas.summary: The main tourist zone stretching north of the town. Dominated by large hotels, apartment complexes, tennis courts, and a long tourist train route connecting to the centre.

areas.name: Savudrija
areas.parking: Generally free or included with accommodation
areas.summary: A quieter, pine-shaded village 8 km north of Umag, known for its active lighthouse. Popular with campers and those seeking a more relaxed pace away from the main resorts.

whenToGo: Umag’s tourist season runs from May to October. July and August are the hottest months with daytime temperatures around 30°C and sea temperatures peaking at 26°C. This is also the most crowded and expensive time, especially during the ATP tennis tournament in late July. June and September offer a better balance of warm weather, lower prices, and fewer crowds, with September sea temperatures still comfortable for swimming. Between November and April, the town is very quiet; most resort hotels, beach bars, and seasonal restaurants close, though the coastal paths remain open for walking and cycling.

faq.question: Is Umag worth visiting?
faq.answer: Yes, especially if you want a resort-style holiday or are driving from Central Europe. It lacks the extensive historical architecture of Rovinj or Poreč, but excels in sports facilities, family resorts, and accessible coastlines.

faq.question: How many days do I need in Umag?
faq.answer: Three to five days is ideal for a standard beach and relaxation trip. If you use it as a base to explore inland Istria or nearby coastal towns, a full week is recommended.

faq.question: What is the best beach in Umag?
faq.answer: Laguna Stella Maris is the most popular, featuring a crescent-shaped pebble and artificial sand shoreline with shallow water. Katoro and Polynesia offer wide concrete terraces and rocky sections with clear water.

faq.question: Do I need a car in Umag?
faq.answer: You do not need a car if you stay within the main resort areas, as a tourist train connects Katoro and Stella Maris to the town centre. However, a car is highly recommended for taking day trips around Istria.

faq.question: Where can I park in Umag?
faq.answer: The town operates a zoned public parking system, with large paid lots located near the bus station and marina, just outside the pedestrian old town. Most large hotels and resorts further north include parking, though some charge a daily fee.

faq.question: Is Umag good for families?
faq.answer: Yes, Umag is one of the most family-friendly destinations in Istria. The northern resorts offer dedicated children's animation, shallow beach sections, playgrounds, and large pool complexes tailored to young visitors.
